transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been having thoughts that it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And driving home from the clinic, I sometimes catch myself wondering what would happen if I just… didn’t turn the wheel. That scared me.
How has your mood been feeling overall over the past few weeks?

Most days, I feel really down. It’s like the color has drained out of everything, even when the house is busy. I end up crying in the laundry room sometimes because I can’t stand anyone seeing how hopeless I feel.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt this down or depressed before in your life?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had bad days before, but I can’t really tell you if it was this kind of down.
Have you ever had a time in your life where you felt the opposite—extremely energetic, full of ideas, or needing much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?
There was a stretch when I was sleeping maybe three hours a night, but I’d get up before sunrise feeling completely sharp. I honestly felt like I didn’t need any more sleep.
How long did that period of needing very little sleep and feeling so sharp last?
It was a stretch—I was only sleeping about three hours a night, getting up before sunrise, and still feeling completely sharp. I really thought I didn’t need more rest.
About how many days or weeks did that stretch go on for?
It’s been going on about a month—the whole intense up-and-down crisis around taking in our relative.
During that time when you were sleeping so little, did you feel unusually high, irritable, or on top of the world?

Earlier this month, I felt almost electrically upbeat at first. Then I was snapping at everybody over little things—a misplaced medication cup, a change in the morning schedule. It really didn’t feel like my usual self.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a current depressive episode characterized by persistent low mood, feelings of hopelessness, crying spells, and passive suicidal ideation. Crucially, the patient also reports a distinct preceding period of abnormally elevated/electrically upbeat and irritable mood, accompanied by a markedly decreased need for sleep (sleeping 3 hours a night while feeling completely sharp), consistent with a manic or hypomanic episode. This clinical picture fulfills the criteria for Bipolar affective disorder (F31).

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed mood and feeling that the color has drained out of everything
Passive suicidal ideation and driving-related thoughts of self-harm
Decreased need for sleep (sleeping ~3 hours without fatigue)
Electrically upbeat mood shifting into irritability and snapping at others
